'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Northern Chad offensive|Northern Chad offensive]]
**Rebel forces of the [[Front for Change and Concord in Chad]] advance to the capital, [[N'Djamena]], as incumbent [[President of Chad|President]] [[Idriss Déby]] takes a lead in the April 11 election and is expected to extend his mandate. Yesterday, the U.S. and British governments ordered some [[diplom]]atic staff to leave [[Chad]] amidst the unrest. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-embassy-withdraw-staff-chad-rebels-advance-2021-04-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Niger attacks]]
**At least 19 civilians are killed and two are wounded when armed men raid a village in the [[Tillabéri Region]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/18/nineteen-civilians-killed-in-new-west-niger-attack (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Toukh train accident]]
**A train [[derailment]] in [[Toukh]], [[Qalyubiyya Governorate|Qalyubiyya]], [[Egypt]], leaves at least 11 people dead and another 98 injured. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2021/04/18/At-least-eight-killed-as-train-derails-in-Egypt (Al Arabiya English)]
*[[2021 Table Mountain fire]]
**[[Mostert's Mill]] in [[Cape Town]], South Africa, is destroyed by a fire that spread from [[Table Mountain]]. [https://twitter.com/Newzroom405/status/1383775230284292104 (Newzroom Afrika via Twitter)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-56793317 (BBC News)]
*A [[Richter magnitude scale|magnitude]] 5.9 earthquake strikes the [[Bushehr Province]] in southern [[Iran]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-xl/middleeast/top-stories/magnitude-5-9-earthquake-hits-southern-iran-no-casualties-reported-tv/ar-BB1fM1t8 (Reuters via MSN)]
*A crash in the [[Eastern Cape]] of South Africa kills seven people when their vehicle collides with head on with a bus. [https://www.enca.com/news/7-die-n2-head-collision (eNCA)]
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****India reports a record 261,500 new confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 14.78 million. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/another-peak-in-india-s-daily-covid-19-count-261-500-fresh-infections-take-tall-101618717546050.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] lifts its outdoor [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask mandate]] and fully reopens schools as the number of COVID-19 cases reduces and the majority of the population is [[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel|vaccinated]]. However, masks must still be worn in indoor public spaces. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-lifts-outdoor-mask-mandate-fully-reopens-schools/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 1,340 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 21,995. [https://m.akipress.com/news:657000:Mongolia_reports_1,340_new_cases_of_coronavirus,_3_deaths/ (AKIPress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] reports 149 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total this year. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2295438/pakistan-records-years-highest-single-day-covid-19-death-toll (Tribune)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 1,767 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 42,352. The nationwide death toll also surpasses 100. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2101363/thailand-logs-2-deaths-record-1-767-covid-cases-sunday (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
***[[Turkey]] reports a record 318 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 35,926. [https://apnews.com/article/pandemics-turkey-coronavirus-pandemic-51616e9efa1032384fa2282efc499261 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vanuatu]]
***[[Vanuatu]] halts outbound travel out of its main island of [[Efate]] following the confirmation of a COVID-19 case. Prime Minister [[Bob Loughman]] confirms that a Filipino fisherman whose body washed ashore last week near the capital of [[Port Vila]] had died of the disease.  [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/440739/vanuatu-s-main-island-halts-outward-travel-after-covid-discovery (RNZ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The daughter of [[opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|Russian opposition]] leader [[Alexei Navalny]] calls on Russian authorities to allow doctors to check on her father, a day after doctors warned he could "die within days" from [[cardiac arrest]] or [[kidney failure]]. Navalny has been on a [[hunger strike]] since March in protest of prison medical conditions. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/daughter-jailed-kremlin-critic-alexei-navalny-says-he-needs-doctor-2021-04-18/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-56786266 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Cape Verdean parliamentary election]]
**Voters in [[Cape Verde]] go to the polls to elect new members of the [[National Assembly (Cape Verde)|National Assembly]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/04/17/cape-verde-final-colourful-campaigns-before-parliamentary-election/ (''Africanews'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[European Super League|The Super League]]
**In a major move, six [[Premier League]] teams: [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], as well as several European clubs such as [[FC Barcelona]] and [[Juventus F.C.|Juventus]], agree to join The Super League, an annual club competition for the "elite teams" of Europe. [[UEFA]] and [[FIFA]] condemn the announcement, saying that they will not recognize the competition, and that players who take part in the competition will be banned from all other [[association football|football]] competitions, including representing their national side at the [[FIFA World Cup]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56795811 (BBC News)]
